In short - It's brilliant, especially if you play it with someone that means a lot to you. The type of game that really makes you appreciate the hobby.

What I loved:
- This game is a visual feast, with each chapter taking place in different but equally lovingly crafted environments. From start to finish there were moments where I was completely blown away and just had to stop whatever we were doing to look around because I was blown away.
- Controls and camera felt smooth as silk, and the movement felt great. So often games like this are undone by janky mechanics, which is not the case here.
- Throughout, everything felt truly collaborative rather than being two paralell stories that converged from time to time. You couldn't play this game without communicating, and that's the way it should be.
- While the story wasn't anything groundbreaking it did hit the emotional notes it was going for well, and the gameplay did a great job of balancing the seriousness of the predicament you're in with the levity that comes with suddenly being dropped into these tiny, absurd worlds. My personal favourite moment was finding a full service day spa run by bugs!
- The characters themselves were great and although each had their moments of being annoying there was no one in this story that had me rolling my eyes every time they were on screen. Everyone played a key role and did it well.

What I wasn't a huge fan of:
- The underpinning story felt very safe and predictable. Again, it hits the emotional notes it intends to well enough but I think there were some opportunities to kick it up a notch that weren't taken. E.g. The therapy sessions between the main characters could have been a touch longer and more reflective rather than just one key insight snark fests.
- I could just be an idiot who couldn't figure it out, but I'm unsure whether this game had a localised chat option. While this is easily solved using Discord or something similar, if this actually is the case then it's a puzzling decision considering this game requires the two players to communicate constantly to succeed. More than that, the chat between the action sequences and the inside jokes that we formed through out idle banter enriched my experience of the game significantly, and I couldn't imagine you'd get nearly as much from a playthrough where you weren't able to talk to eachother.

Overall:
- How would I rate it?: 9/10
- Would I play it again?: Absolutely
- Would I buy it at full price?: Yes, in a heartbeat.

My wife says this is the best game she's ever seen by far.  It is the only game that I have ever seen her actually want to play.  Absolutely fantastic to experience together as a couple.  The variety in the gameplay is astounding, so much so that even though it is not punishing, which is favorable to a non gamer, someone who games a lot won't get bored.  The visuals are happy and uplifting, and make you feel like a kid.  Some parts are hilariously dark mixed with light and fluffy.  Hazelight found the secret sauce, and cooked a masterpiece.

As you play, your significant other gradually transforms from a teammate into a sparring partner—someone who might not only casually punch your lights out but also make you question why you decided to play together in the first place. Expect shouting, mutual accusations, and lines like "WHERE ARE YOU JUMPING?!", "BUT I PRESSED THE BUTTON!", and the classic "THAT'S IT, I'M NOT PLAYING WITH YOU ANYMORE!" But the real fun begins after the final credits roll. That’s when you’ll realize just how well you can work as a team, forgive mistakes, and keep your cool when your partner messes everything up yet again. 

Verdict: 10/10—a simulator that tests both your nerves and your relationship.
